catalog_quote: जहाँ तक अक्षर बलाघात का सम्बन्ध है, कुलुई में इसकी विभिन्न प्रवृत्तियाँ हैं। (1) एकाक्षरी शब्द सभी बलाघात्मक होते हैं, और इन में व्यंजन की अपेक्षा स्वर पर अधिक बल होता है—खा', पी', जा', आ'ण, शु'ण आदि। ... जब ये अकेले बोले जाएँ तो ये पूर्ण बलाघात हैं, वाक्य में प्रयोग होने से बलाघात बदल सकता है। (2) द्व्यक्षरी (disyllabic) शब्दों की स्थिति में प्रायः मुख्य (primary) बलाघात दूसरे अक्षर पर पड़ता है, तथा प्रथम अक्षर पर गौण (secondary) बलाघात रहता है। "शोठा" शब्द में 'ठा' पर मुख्य बल है और 'शो' पर गौण—शोठा'। इसी तरह कोठा', घाणी', काठू', शाब'र, लाब'र, बाणा', चोखा', चीक'र, ... नुहा'र, भाऊ', ... आदि। (3) तीन अक्षरों वाले शब्दों में प्रायः मध्य अक्षर पर मुख्य बलाघात होता है, अन्तिम पर गौण और प्रथम पर तृतीयक (tertiary) बलाघात होता है। पाहुणा शब्द में ये बलाघात क्रमशः 'हु', 'णा' और 'पा' पर हैं। इसी तरह धाउ'ड़ा, पाइ'रा, गोझी'णा, पिया'णा, शौगी'णा आदि। बहु-अक्षरी शब्दों में प्रायः दूसरे अक्षर पर मुख्य बलाघात रहता है—जैसे फका'हुका, बज़ा'हिणा, बझ'रना, चुना'हड़ा, मठि'याई, पनशा'कड़ा, आदि। कुलुई में उपर्युक्त अक्षर बलाघात निरर्थक हैं। इनसे शब्दों के अर्थ में अन्तर नहीं आता। यदि बोलने वाला बलाघात के इन निश्चित स्थानों की अपेक्षा किसी और अक्षर पर बल डाले तो इनके अर्थ में भेद नहीं आता।

new_statements.translation: As regards syllable stress, Kului shows the following tendencies. (1) Monosyllabic words are all stressed ... (2) In disyllabic words the primary stress usually falls on the second syllable, and secondary stress remains on the first syllable. In the word śoṭhā the main force is on ṭhā and the secondary on śo ... (3) In words of three syllables the primary stress is usually on the middle syllable, secondary on the last and tertiary on the first. In the word pāhuṇā these stresses are on hu, ṇā and pā respectively. ... In polysyllabic words the primary stress usually remains on the second syllable ... In Kului the above syllable stresses are non-significant: they make no difference to the meaning of words.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Kului is non-contrastive and (usually) falls on the second syllable of the word: final syllable in disyllables (śoṭhā', koṭhā', ghāṇī', śāb'r, cīk'r), medial syllable in trisyllables (pāhu'ṇā, dhāu'ṛā, piyā'ṇā), second syllable in longer words (phakā'hukā, bazā'hiṇā, maṭhi'yāī, panśā'kaṛā); monosyllables bear full stress in isolation. Adding a syllable shifts the stress accordingly (śoṭ 'throw!' vs śoṭū' 'threw'). Consistent with this, an unstressed word-initial short vowel is commonly dropped (abhyās > bhyās, anāj > nāj, ilāj > lāj; pp. 185-186), a process Ranganatha 1980 p. 85 also records (optional loss of initial-syllable /ə/).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Thakur grades stress: in disyllables secondary stress on the first syllable; in trisyllables secondary on the final syllable and tertiary on the first. Nothing said about secondary stress in words of four or more syllables beyond primary on the second.
new_statements.exceptions: All rules hedged with 'prāyaḥ' (usually); author says a speaker stressing a different syllable causes no change of meaning. Sentence (word-in-phrase) stress is free and pragmatic. Separately (surāghāt, pp. 188-189) he reports limited pitch/tone contrasts: level vs (high-/low-)falling pitch distinguishes some word pairs (sān 'easy' vs sān 'favour', pūlā 'bundle' vs 'grass shoe', seū 'apple' vs 'bridge', ghaṛin 'stench' vs 'clod'), and a rising contour on the final word marks yes/no questions; he states tone in Kului is 'not so clear and widespread' as in Chinese. LSI-HP 2023 lists only nasalisation and length as suprasegmental phonemes.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern the word in isolation (citation forms); Thakur notes monosyllables are fully stressed 'when spoken alone' and that stress may change in connected speech; sentence-level prominence treated separately as śabda-balāghāt. Impressionistic (no instrumental data).
new_statements.identity_note: Thakur 1975 describes Kului proper (upper Beas/Kullu valley speech; the author is a native speaker from Kullu) and treats Outer Siraji and Inner Siraji as sub-dialects in a separate chapter; the stress rules are stated for 'Kului'. This is the same variety as Glottolog kull1236 / ISO kfx (Ranganatha 1980 'Kului', LSI-HP 2023 'Kulvi'). Note the earlier scan's named source (Hendriksen 1986 Himachali Studies III) does NOT describe Kului: it treats Kotgarhi and Koci (Shimla district varieties) and merely cites Thakur 1975 for Kului data.
